lines.text: When the night is darkest and the cold bites hardest, one voice still rises to greet the dawn — the Gallic Rooster, who crows loudest when all others fall silent. France does not fear the dark.
But deep in the Nordic forests something stirs — the Lindworm, the great wingless dragon of old, patient and cold-blooded. Tonight, the rooster meets the dragon.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-two. France, versus Sweden. A knockout. Win, or the dragon swallows your summer whole.
France arrive as giants — world champions, finalists, the land of Zidane and Mbappé. Sweden arrive as the dark horse with venom up front, the team nobody wants to draw.
France — Les Bleus. Elegant, devastating, ruthless. A team with more firepower than almost anyone alive.
Kylian Mbappé is lightning made flesh, the fastest finisher on earth. Antoine Griezmann is the brain, the leader who makes it all tick. And Ousmane Dembélé terrifies full-backs with both feet.
Aurélien Tchouaméni shields and strides from deep like a colossus. And William Saliba is ice at the back, calm under any storm.
Sweden — Blågult, the blue and gold. Organised, fearless, and armed with two of the most lethal strikers in Europe.
Viktor Gyökeres is a battering ram who scores for fun. Alexander Isak glides like silk and finishes like a dream. And Dejan Kulusevski drives them forward with power and guile.
Anthony Elanga burns the turf with raw pace. And Victor Lindelöf, the captain, marshals the dragon's scales at the back.
So here is the riddle. Can the rooster crow over a giant of his own? Or does the Lindworm coil around France and squeeze the life from the favourites?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a single flash of lightning.
Here is how we see it. Sweden come out cold and clinical — no fear of the badge, no respect for reputation — and France are rocked.
The dragon strikes first. The forest goes quiet, and the favourites are staring at the abyss.
And it lands. Viktor Gyökeres bullies his way through and finishes ruthlessly. Sweden lead. The Lindworm has drawn blood.
But you do not silence the rooster so easily. France stir. Griezmann starts to pull the strings, and the lightning begins to gather.
And Kylian Mbappé erupts. One touch, one blur of blue, and it is buried. One — one. The rooster crows.
And then, late, the lightning strikes twice. Mbappé again — too fast, too cold, too good. Two — one, France. The dragon is slain.
Two — one. Sweden were magnificent, and frightening, and so nearly there — but Mbappé is a different kind of monster. The rooster crows over the dawn.
Our prediction — France two, Sweden one. Mbappé, a brace, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Sweden leave with their heads high — the dragon that nearly toppled a giant, undone only by a single bolt of lightning.
France march on. Les Bleus, reminding the world that when the night is darkest, the rooster still crows the loudest.
So you tell me — the rooster, or the dragon? Comment FRANCE for Les Bleus — comment SWEDEN for the dragon of the north.

Across the fields of France they tell of the golden rooster on the spire — the one who fears no night, no storm, no giant, and crows defiance into the dark until the sun returns. Legend eighty-two — the Gallic Rooster, Herald of the Dawn.
The players write the night. But the Gallic Rooster carries one truth — courage is not crowing when the sun is up. It is crowing when the night says you cannot.
